title: Living in urban, rural and remote places

match.reason: The closest bank point, geo-urban-remote-australia, covers lower wellbeing, incomes and services in remote areas, but it does not teach the brief's trade-off of city jobs and services against higher living costs and rural space and community, so no bank point teaches the same idea.

draft.title: Living in urban, rural and remote places
card: Urban
in cities and large towns. People have many jobs, schools, hospitals and shops close by. Housing and living costs are usually higher, and there is more traffic and crowding.
Rural
in farming areas and small towns. There is more open space and often a close community. Services such as specialist doctors can be further away.
Remote
far from large towns, with very few people. Services are the fewest here, and people may travel long distances or use online services for school and health.
Each type of place has benefits and costs. What suits a person depends on their job, family and what they value.
draft.remember: Cities offer jobs and services at a higher cost. Rural and remote places offer space and community, with fewer services.

a.q: Which is most likely to be a challenge of living in a remote place?
opts: Long distances to reach services
Very high rents and house prices
Heavy traffic on most roads
Crowded public transport
a.why: Remote places have few people and few services, so travel to reach them can be long. High rents, traffic and crowded transport are more typical of cities.
a.clue: Remote means far from large towns.

b.q: Sam works as a nurse and wants a wide choice of jobs and a hospital nearby. Which place suits Sam best, and what is the likely cost?
opts: A city, but with higher living costs
A remote place, but with higher living costs
A city, but with fewer services nearby
A remote place, but with fewer jobs to choose from
b.why: Cities have many jobs and hospitals close by, but costs such as housing are usually higher. A remote place has fewer jobs and services, so it does not meet what Sam wants, even though it offers space.
b.clue: Match what Sam wants to where jobs and hospitals are found.

b.best: A city, but with higher living costs

problems.detail: The Urban line says living costs are usually higher in cities. In Australia that holds for housing, but everyday costs such as food, fuel and transport are often higher in remote places. Narrow it to housing costs, or say that remote places can have high costs for goods.

The remember line says rural and remote places both offer community and gives city costs as simply higher. The card only says rural areas often have a close community, says nothing about community in remote places, and says city costs are usually higher. The line sorts the ideas more neatly than the card does.

check.summary: Both questions work and each has a single clear answer. The card's claim that living costs are usually higher in cities overlooks the high cost of goods in remote Australia, and the remember line drops 'usually' and gives remote places a community the card does not mention.
